title: Account Fare Volume Terms for Late Enrollment Bonuses under Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements
content:
**Term.** For an enrollment bonus on a Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements agreement, the enrollment fare measure is the total of the fares collected on the company's tickets, placed by collection date, in the enrollment fare window of 12 calendar months up to and including the credit date — every fare collection in the fare ledger of the company's tickets under Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand. The enrollment-bonus lateness is the number of whole calendar months from the agreement's approval date to the credit date. A late enrollment bonus earns a fare uplift:

| Lateness | Enrollment fare measure | Fare uplift |
|---|---|---|
| 6 months or more | USD 100000 or more | 10 percentage points |
| 6 months or more | USD 50000 or more, below 100000 | 5 percentage points |
| 6 months or more | below USD 50000 | none |
| fewer than 6 months | any | none |

**How the uplift acts.** The uplift is counted in percentage points; enrollment-bonus uplifts on different grounds are added together, and the enrollment bonus is raised by the total: the bonus before allowances is the enrollment bonus multiplied by one hundred plus the total uplift, divided by one hundred, rounded down to the whole point.

### Questions on the terms

**Do fares paid by card count toward the measure?** Yes. Every fare collected on the company's tickets counts, whatever the form of payment.

**What does an enrollment bonus of 2500 points become with a fare uplift of 5 percentage points and no other uplift? (hypothetical)** 2500 multiplied by 105 and divided by one hundred: 2625 points before allowances.

**Does a fare collected 13 months before the credit date count?** No; only collections inside the 12-month window count.
